Surah al-Jathiyah (Surah 45) [Meccan, except for six or seven of its verses, which are thirty-seven in number]

﴿Ha, Mim.﴾ Allah knows best what He means by it.

﴿The revelation of the Book﴾, meaning the Qur'an, is the *mubtada'* (مُبْتَدَأ, the grammatical subject of the nominal sentence). ﴿From Allah﴾ is its *khabar* (خَبَره, the predicate). ﴿The All-Mighty﴾ is in His dominion, and ﴿the All-Wise﴾ is in His creation.

Verse 3 of Surah 45 (al-Jathiyah) with the commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti:

﴿Indeed, in the heavens and the earth﴾, i.e., in their creation, ﴿are signs﴾ indicating the power of God and His oneness, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 45, verse 4:

﴿And in your creation﴾, i.e., in the creation of each of you, from a drop (nutfah), then a clinging clot (alaqah), then a lump of flesh (mudghah), until he becomes a human being. ﴿And what He scatters﴾ means what He disperses throughout the earth ﴿of living creatures﴾, meaning what crawls upon the earth, of humankind and others. ﴿are signs for a people who have certainty﴾ concerning the Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 45, verse 5:

﴿And﴾ in ﴿the alternation of the night and the day﴾ their going and their coming, ﴿and in what Allah sends down from the sky of provision﴾ rain, because it is the cause of provision, ﴿and by it He gives life to the earth after its death, and in the turning of the winds﴾ their being turned, once southward and once northward, and cold and hot, ﴿are signs for a people who use reason﴾ the proof, so that they believe.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 45, verse 6:

﴿These﴾ — the aforementioned verses — ﴿are the verses of Allah﴾, His proofs indicating His oneness, ﴿which We recite﴾, i.e. relate, ﴿to you in truth﴾: this is connected to "We recite" (natluhā). ﴿Then in what statement after Allah﴾, i.e. after His statement, which is the Qur'an, ﴿and His verses﴾, His proofs, ﴿will they believe?﴾ That is, the disbelievers of Makkah — meaning they do not believe. And in one reading it is read with the letter ta' (tu'minūna, "will you believe?").

Woe (ويل) is a word for punishment, for every ifak (أفّاك, one who lies persistently), sinful (أثيم), meaning one who commits much sin.

Woe (wayl) is a word denoting punishment, for every ʾaffāk (أفّاك, persistent liar), who is kadhdhāb (كَذّاب, a great liar) and athīm (أثيم, one who commits much sin).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 45, verse 8:

﴿Who hears the verses of Allah﴾, the Qur'an, ﴿recited to him, then persists﴾ in his disbelief ﴿arrogantly﴾, being proud (mutakabbiran) of faith, ﴿as though he did not hear them. So give him good tidings of a painful punishment﴾, painful (mu'lim).

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn, a concise commentary) on surah 45, verse 9:**

﴿And when he learns something of Our verses﴾, i.e. the Qur'an, ﴿something﴾, ﴿he takes them in mockery﴾, i.e. made the object of mockery through them. ﴿Those﴾, i.e. the liars, ﴿for them is a humiliating punishment﴾, meaning one that involves humiliation.

﴿Behind them﴾, i.e., in front of them, because they are in this world. ﴿Hell﴾. ﴿Nor will avail them what they earned﴾ of wealth and deeds ﴿anything, nor those they took as protectors besides Allah﴾, i.e., the idols.

This is the Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 45, verse 11:

﴿This﴾ i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿is a guidance﴾ from misguidance. ﴿As for those who disbelieve in the signs of their Lord, for them is a punishment﴾ a portion ﴿of a painful torment﴾ i.e., a punishment, ﴿painful﴾ causing pain.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 45, verse 12:

﴿Allah is the One who subjected the sea to you, that the ships may sail upon it by His command﴾ — "the ships" (al-fulk) means the vessels — "by His command" means by His permission — "and that you may seek" means seek, through trade,

And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens — the sun, the moon, the stars, water and other things — and whatever is on the earth — animals, trees, plants, rivers and other things. That is, He created all of that for your benefit. ﴿all of it﴾ is an emphasis (ta'kid). ﴿from Him﴾ is a circumstantial clause (hal), meaning: He subjected them as a bounty proceeding from Him, may He be exalted. ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect﴾ upon them, so that they believe.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 45, verse 14:

﴿Say to those who believe: forgive those who do not expect the Days of Allah﴾ (who do not fear) ﴿the Days of Allah﴾ (its events), meaning: forgive the disbelievers the harm they have inflicted upon you. This was before the command to fight them (jihad against them). ﴿So that He may recompense﴾ (i.e., Allah; in another reading, with the letter nun) ﴿a people for what they used to earn﴾ (from forgiving the disbelievers their harm).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 45, verse 15:

﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own soul﴾ (i.e., he did it), ﴿and whoever does evil, it is against it﴾ (i.e., he did it), ﴿then to your Lord you will be returned﴾ (i.e., you will go back), so He will recompense the righteous doer and the evildoer.

﴿And We had certainly given the Children of Israel the Book﴾, which is the Torah, ﴿and the judgment﴾ by it among the people, ﴿and prophethood﴾ for Musa and Harun from among them, ﴿and We provided for them of the good things﴾, meaning the lawful things, such as the manna and the quails, ﴿and We preferred them over the worlds﴾, meaning the worlds of their time, the rational beings.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 45, verse 17:

﴿And We gave them clear proofs concerning the matter﴾ — the matter of the religion, [concerning] the lawful and the unlawful, and the sending of Muhammad ﷺ, upon whom be the best of prayers and peace. ﴿And they did not differ﴾ concerning his mission ﴿except after knowledge had come to them, out of envy among themselves﴾ — i.e., due to an envy that arose among them, jealousy of him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 45, verse 18:

﴿Then We placed you﴾ O Muhammad ﴿on a path (sharia)﴾ meaning a way ﴿of the affair﴾ the affair of the religion ﴿so follow it, and do not follow the desires of those who do not know﴾ in worshipping other than Allah.

Surah 45, verse 19 (Tafsir al-Jalalayn):

﴿Indeed, they will not avail you﴾ (yadfa'ū, i.e. ward off) ﴿against Allah in anything﴾ (min 'adhābihi, i.e. from His punishment) ﴿shay'an﴾. ﴿And indeed, the wrongdoers﴾ (al-kāfirīn, i.e. the disbelievers) ﴿are allies of one another, but Allah is the Ally of the righteous.﴾

This is the Qur'an: ﴿This﴾ Qur'an is ﴿insights for mankind﴾, landmarks by which they gain insight regarding the laws and the limits, ﴿and a guidance and a mercy for a people who have certainty﴾ concerning the Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 45, verse 21:

﴿Am﴾ here means the interrogative particle of denial (hamzat al-inkar). ﴿Do those who commit evil deeds (ijtarahu al-sayyi'at)﴾ acquire (iktasabu) ﴿evil deeds﴾, namely disbelief and sins, ﴿suppose that We will make them like those who believe and do righteous deeds, equal﴾ (sawa'). The predicate (khabar) is ﴿their living and their dying﴾, which is the subject (mubtada') and a conjoined element (ma'tuf), and the clause is a substitute (badal) for the kaf (the "them" in "make them like"). The two pronouns refer to the disbelievers. The meaning is: Do they suppose that We will make them, in the Hereafter, in a state of good like the believers, in a pleasant life equal to their life in this world, since they said to the believers: "If we are raised again, we will surely be given good like what you are given"? Allah the Exalted responded in line with their denial, which is expressed by the hamza: ﴿Evil is what they judge﴾, i.e., the matter is not so; rather, they will be in the Hereafter in punishment, contrary to their life in this world, while the believers in the Hereafter will be in reward for their righteous deeds in this world, such as prayer, zakat, fasting and other things. The ma here is a verbal-source particle (masdariyya), meaning: wretched is the judgment this judgment of theirs is.

Translation of the commentary (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 45, verse 22:

﴿And Allah created the heavens and the earth with truth﴾: the phrase "with truth" is connected to "created," so that it points to His power and His oneness. ﴿And that every soul may be recompensed for what it has earned﴾: from sins and acts of obedience, so that the disbeliever is not made equal to the believer.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 45, verse 23:

﴿Have you seen﴾ tell me ﴿him who takes as his god his own desire﴾ whatever he desires of stone after stone, which he sees as better. ﴿And Allah has led him astray knowingly﴾ from Him, exalted is He: i.e., knowing that he is among the people of misguidance before He created him. ﴿And has sealed over his hearing and his heart﴾ so he does not hear guidance nor understand it. ﴿And has put over his sight a covering﴾ darkness, so he does not see guidance. Here the second object of ﴿ra'aytum﴾ is to be understood: "Will he be guided?" ﴿Then who can guide him after Allah?﴾ i.e., after His leading him astray; that is, he will not be guided. ﴿Will you not then take heed?﴾ admonish yourselves. Here the idgham (assimilation) of one of the two taʾs into the dhal occurs.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 45, verse 24:**

﴿And they said﴾, i.e. the deniers of the resurrection (al-ba'th), ﴿"It is not but our life﴾, i.e. life, ﴿"the worldly life"﴾ which is in ﴿the world. We die and we live﴾, i.e. some of us die and some of us live, by being born. ﴿"And nothing destroys us but time (ad-dahr)"﴾, i.e. the passing of time. ﴿And they have no knowledge of that﴾, the said statement, ﴿"[that] in"﴾ (إنْ) meaning ﴿"ma"﴾ (ما)

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 45, verse 25:

﴿And when Our verses are recited to them﴾ from the Qur'an, which indicate Our power to resurrect, ﴿clear﴾ evident, a ḥāl (circumstantial qualifier) of the verses. ﴿Their argument was only that they said, "Bring back our forefathers"﴾ alive, ﴿if you are truthful﴾ that we will be resurrected.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 45, verse 26:

﴿Say: "Allah gives you life﴾ when you were drops of semen, ﴿then causes you to die, then gathers you﴾ alive ﴿on the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt﴾ (no uncertainty) ﴿in it. But most people﴾ (are those who say what has been mentioned) ﴿do not know.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 45, verse 27:

﴿And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And the Day the Hour is established – that Day the falsifiers will be lost.﴾ [The phrase] "that Day" (yawma'idhin) is a substitute (badal) for "the Day" (yawm) [in the preceding clause]. "The falsifiers" (al-mubtilun) are the disbelievers, meaning: their loss will become manifest, by their being brought to the Fire.

﴿And you will see every community﴾, i.e., every people of a religion, ﴿kneeling﴾ upon their knees, or ﴿gathered together﴾. ﴿Every community will be called to its record﴾, the record of its deeds. And it will be said to them, ﴿Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do﴾, i.e., its recompense.

This is the commentary on Qur'an 45:29, which reads: "This is Our Record; it speaks against you with truth. Indeed, We were having transcribed what you used to do."

"This is Our Record" (the register of the guardian angels) "speaks against you with truth; indeed, We were having transcribed (nastansikh)" meaning: We were recording and preserving.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 45, verse 30:

﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, their Lord will admit them into His mercy﴾ (i.e., His Paradise) ﴿That is the clear triumph﴾ (al-bayyin, i.e., the evident, manifest one)

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 45, verse 31:

﴿And as for those who disbelieved﴾ it will be said to them, ﴿"Were not My verses recited to you? But you were arrogant﴾ (takabbartum, you became proud) ﴿and you were a people of criminals﴾ (kafirin, disbelievers).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 45, verse 32:

﴿And when it was said﴾ to you, O disbelievers, ﴿that the promise of Allah﴾ of resurrection ﴿is true, and the Hour﴾ is read with both the nominative and the accusative ﴿- there is no doubt﴾ (shakk) ﴿concerning it - you said, "We do not know what the Hour is. We only assume it to be a [mere] assumption﴾ - al-Mubarrad said: its original form is, "in naḥnu illā naẓunnu ẓannan" (we are only assuming an assumption) ﴿and we are not certain﴾ that it is coming.

﴿And there will appear to them﴾ (i.e., become manifest) in the Hereafter ﴿the evils of what they did﴾ in the world, i.e., their recompense. ﴿And there will befall them﴾ (i.e., descend upon them) ﴿what they used to mock﴾, i.e., the punishment.

{And it will be said, "Today We forget you," meaning, We leave you in the Fire, "as you forgot the meeting of this your Day," meaning, you abandoned the works for its meeting. "Your abode is the Fire, and you have no helpers," meaning, protectors preventing you from it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 45, verse 35:

﴿That is because you took the signs of Allah﴾ the Qur'an ﴿as mockery, and the worldly life deceived you﴾ until you said, "There is no resurrection and no reckoning." ﴿So today they will not be brought out﴾ — read with the verb in the active or the passive voice — ﴿from it﴾ from the Fire, ﴿nor will they be asked to make amends﴾ — it is not demanded of them that they please their Lord through repentance and obedience, because these will not benefit them on that Day.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn: the passage is a short gloss, so I translate it directly.

﴿So to Allah belongs all praise﴾ the ascribing of what is beautiful to Him for the fulfilment of His promise concerning the deniers, ﴿Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of the worlds﴾ the Creator of what has been mentioned, and "the worlds" (al-ʿalam) is everything other than Allah; it is made plural because of the difference in its kinds, and "Lord" (rabb) is a substitution (badal).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 45, verse 37:

﴿And to Him belongs the greatness﴾ (al-Kibriya'), i.e., the majesty, ﴿in the heavens and the earth﴾. This is a circumstantial phrase (hal): meaning, existing within them. ﴿And He is the Almighty, the All-Wise﴾. This has already been explained.
